1. Assignment Overview and Learning Objectives¶

By completing A3, you should be able to build a reproducible classification pipeline; prepare datasets and augmentation; perform frozen transfer and full fine-tuning; compare architectures and optimization choices; evaluate class-wise performance; interpret learned embeddings; adapt the pipeline to external, real-world datasets pulled from the Hugging Face Hub; distinguish overfitting from underfitting; and analyze robustness and failures.

Point map: core implementation 50; required experiments and evidence 46 (31 core comparisons, 15 real-world transfer on Hugging Face datasets); analysis and interpretation 14 (4 synthesis, 10 failure analysis); reproducibility, organization, and submission compliance 5; extension 10.

The five categories sum to 125.

3. Dataset and Problem Setup¶

The bundled, balanced CC0 dataset has six visual-pattern classes and fixed 720/180/180 train/validation/test splits. The two local state dictionaries provide offline ImageNet transfer learning. Use validation evidence for every model-selection decision; reserve test data for final evaluation and the required robustness comparison.

Experiments 8 and 9 (Section 5) additionally use two real-world datasets pulled from the Hugging Face Hub with the datasets library: marmal88/skin_cancer (7 diagnostic classes) and timm/eurosat-rgb (10 land-use classes). EuroSAT uses its published train/validation/test splits; Skin Cancer uses lesion-level splits built by a provided helper (Experiment 8). Downloading these two named datasets is the one approved exception to the fully offline policy — do not request any other network resource, and continue to use only the bundled local pretrained weights for the model. The first download is large (about 3.7 GB for Skin Cancer, which needs roughly 7 GB of free disk once datasets builds its local cache, and about 90 MB for EuroSAT), so start it early; later runs reuse the cache.

datasets is the only new package this requires. If your cs5243 environment predates it, you do not need to rebuild the whole environment — conda activate cs5243 and pip install datasets is enough (see README.md).

Implement reusable graded functions in src/student_code.py; use the notebook to run experiments, save artifacts, and explain results. Maintain one cumulative outputs/tables/experiment_metrics.csv.

4. Core Implementation¶

Task 1 — deterministic data pipeline (10 points)¶

Implement build_dataloaders. Build deterministic train/validation/test loaders for the bundled NPZ dataset (a3_tools.dataset_path(), data/dataset/visual_patterns.npz), which stores RGB uint8 arrays train_images, validation_images, and test_images (N×64×64×3) with integer labels train_labels, validation_labels, and test_labels. Return a dictionary with keys train, validation, and test whose loaders yield (images, labels) batches. augmentation must be none, moderate, or strong and applies only to training; evaluation transforms must be deterministic and use ImageNet normalization. Train shuffling must be controlled by seed.

Task 2 — offline pretrained model construction (10 points)¶

Implement build_model. Build mobilenet_v3_small or efficientnet_b0 (the required architecture names) with the bundled local ImageNet state dictionary (a3_tools.weight_path(architecture)): load the state dictionary before replacing the final classifier for num_classes. Do not request network downloads.

In [4]:
for architecture in sc.SUPPORTED_ARCHITECTURES:
    model = sc.build_model(architecture, NUM_CLASSES, a3_tools.weight_path(architecture))
    counts = a3_tools.parameter_counts(model)
    # Compare before any forward pass: a train-mode forward updates BatchNorm running statistics.
    reference = torch.load(a3_tools.weight_path(architecture), map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    backbone_keys = [key for key in reference if key.startswith("features.")]
    loaded = all(torch.equal(model.state_dict()[key], reference[key]) for key in backbone_keys)
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(torch.zeros(2, 3, sc.IMAGE_SIZE, sc.IMAGE_SIZE))
    head = model.classifier[-1]
    print({"architecture": architecture, "logits": tuple(logits.shape),
           "replaced_head": f"Linear({head.in_features} -> {head.out_features})",
           "total_params": f"{counts['total']:,}", "trainable_params": f"{counts['trainable']:,}",
           "backbone_matches_local_weights": loaded, "downloaded_anything": False})

Task 3 — freezing, training, and evaluation (15 points)¶

Implement freeze_backbone, train_one_epoch, and evaluate_model. freeze_backbone freezes every parameter except the replacement classification head. train_one_epoch trains for one complete epoch and returns sample-weighted loss and accuracy. evaluate_model evaluates without gradients and returns loss, accuracy, labels, predictions, and probabilities.

Task 4 — prediction and classification metrics (9 points)¶

Implement predict and classification_metrics. predict returns a dictionary with CPU predictions and softmax probabilities for one image batch. classification_metrics returns a dictionary with confusion_matrix (rows are true classes, columns are predicted classes), overall accuracy, and per-class arrays precision, recall, f1, and per_class_accuracy in class_names order; per-class accuracy is TP_i / (TP_i + FN_i), numerically identical to per-class recall for this single-label task — report both values.

5. Required Experiments¶

The next cell defines the shared harness used by every experiment: a cumulative long-form metrics recorder, a single run_training routine that selects the reported epoch by validation accuracy, inference timing, and plotting helpers. Centralizing it is what keeps the comparisons controlled — each experiment varies exactly one factor and everything else (seed, loaders, epoch budget, evaluation protocol) is held fixed.

In [8]:
from PIL import Image
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Subset
from torchvision import transforms

METRICS_PATH = PATHS["tables"] / "experiment_metrics.csv"
METRIC_COLUMNS = ["experiment", "method", "condition", "metric", "value", "units"]
METRIC_ROWS, RUNS = [], {}
EPOCHS = 10
DEFAULT_LR = {"frozen": {"adam": 1e-3, "sgd": 1e-2}, "finetune": {"adam": 1e-4, "sgd": 1e-3}}


def record(experiment, method, condition, metric, value, units):
    """Append one long-form record to the cumulative metrics table."""
    METRIC_ROWS.append({"experiment": experiment, "method": method, "condition": condition,
                        "metric": metric, "value": float(value), "units": units})


def write_metrics():
    """Rewrite outputs/tables/experiment_metrics.csv from every record collected so far."""
    frame = pd.DataFrame(METRIC_ROWS, columns=METRIC_COLUMNS)
    frame.to_csv(METRICS_PATH, index=False)
    return frame


def make_optimizer(name, parameters, lr):
    if name == "adam":
        return torch.optim.Adam(parameters, lr=lr)
    if name == "sgd":
        return torch.optim.SGD(parameters, lr=lr, momentum=0.9)
    raise ValueError(f"unsupported optimizer: {name}")


def run_training(name, *, architecture="mobilenet_v3_small", mode="finetune", augmentation="none",
                 optimizer_name="adam", lr=None, epochs=EPOCHS, seed=SEED, loaders=None,
                 num_classes=None, class_names=None, label_smoothing=0.0, cosine=False, store=True):
    """Train one configuration and keep the epoch with the best VALIDATION accuracy.

    Test data is never read here, so every selection decision rests on validation evidence.
    """
    a3_tools.seed_everything(seed)
    if loaders is None:
        loaders = sc.build_dataloaders(a3_tools.dataset_path(), BATCH_SIZE, augmentation, seed, NUM_WORKERS)
    names = list(class_names or getattr(loaders["train"].dataset, "class_names", CLASS_NAMES))
    num_classes = int(num_classes or len(names))
    model = sc.build_model(architecture, num_classes, a3_tools.weight_path(architecture))
    sc.freeze_backbone(model) if mode == "frozen" else sc.unfreeze_all(model)
    counts = a3_tools.parameter_counts(model)
    learning_rate = DEFAULT_LR[mode][optimizer_name] if lr is None else lr
    optimizer = make_optimizer(optimizer_name, [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad], learning_rate)
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=epochs) if cosine else None
    train_criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(label_smoothing=label_smoothing)
    eval_criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    history, best_val, best_epoch, best_state = [], -1.0, 0, None
    started = time.time()
    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
        train = sc.train_one_epoch(model, loaders["train"], optimizer, train_criterion, DEVICE)
        validation = sc.evaluate_model(model, loaders["validation"], eval_criterion, DEVICE)
        if scheduler is not None:
            scheduler.step()
        history.append({"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": train["loss"], "train_accuracy": train["accuracy"],
                        "val_loss": validation["loss"], "val_accuracy": validation["accuracy"]})
        if validation["accuracy"] > best_val:
            best_val, best_epoch = validation["accuracy"], epoch
            best_state = {key: value.detach().cpu().clone() for key, value in model.state_dict().items()}
    train_seconds = time.time() - started
    if best_state is not None:
        model.load_state_dict(best_state)

    frame = pd.DataFrame(history)
    run = {"name": name, "architecture": architecture, "mode": mode, "augmentation": augmentation,
           "optimizer": optimizer_name, "lr": learning_rate, "epochs": epochs, "seed": seed,
           "label_smoothing": label_smoothing, "cosine": cosine, "num_classes": num_classes,
           "class_names": names, "history": frame, "model": model, "loaders": loaders,
           "parameter_counts": counts, "best_epoch": best_epoch, "best_val_accuracy": best_val,
           "best_val_loss": float(frame.loc[frame["epoch"] == best_epoch, "val_loss"].iloc[0]),
           "final_train_accuracy": float(frame["train_accuracy"].iloc[-1]),
           "final_train_loss": float(frame["train_loss"].iloc[-1]),
           "final_val_accuracy": float(frame["val_accuracy"].iloc[-1]),
           "train_seconds": train_seconds, "seconds_per_epoch": train_seconds / max(epochs, 1),
           "generalization_gap": float(frame["train_accuracy"].iloc[-1]) - best_val,
           "final_gap": float(frame["train_accuracy"].iloc[-1] - frame["val_accuracy"].iloc[-1])}
    if store:
        RUNS[name] = run
    print(f"[{name}] {architecture} | {mode} | aug={augmentation} | {optimizer_name} lr={learning_rate:g}"
          f" | best val acc {best_val:.4f} @ epoch {best_epoch} | final train acc {run['final_train_accuracy']:.4f}"
          f" | gap {run['generalization_gap']:+.4f} | trainable {counts['trainable']:,} | {train_seconds:.1f}s")
    return run


def record_run(experiment, method, run, *, extra=None):
    """Write the standard block of evidence for one training run."""
    condition = run["name"]
    fields = {"best_val_accuracy": (run["best_val_accuracy"], "fraction"),
              "best_val_loss": (run["best_val_loss"], "cross-entropy"),
              "final_train_accuracy": (run["final_train_accuracy"], "fraction"),
              "final_train_loss": (run["final_train_loss"], "cross-entropy"),
              "generalization_gap": (run["generalization_gap"], "fraction"),
              "selected_epoch": (run["best_epoch"], "epoch"),
              "total_parameters": (run["parameter_counts"]["total"], "count"),
              "trainable_parameters": (run["parameter_counts"]["trainable"], "count"),
              "train_wall_time": (run["train_seconds"], "seconds"),
              "seconds_per_epoch": (run["seconds_per_epoch"], "seconds")}
    fields.update(extra or {})
    for metric, (value, units) in fields.items():
        record(experiment, method, condition, metric, value, units)


def summarize(names):
    """Comparison table for a set of stored runs."""
    return pd.DataFrame([{"run": RUNS[n]["name"], "architecture": RUNS[n]["architecture"], "mode": RUNS[n]["mode"],
                          "augmentation": RUNS[n]["augmentation"], "optimizer": RUNS[n]["optimizer"],
                          "lr": RUNS[n]["lr"], "best_val_acc": RUNS[n]["best_val_accuracy"],
                          "best_val_loss": RUNS[n]["best_val_loss"],
                          "final_train_acc": RUNS[n]["final_train_accuracy"],
                          "gap": RUNS[n]["generalization_gap"],
                          "trainable": RUNS[n]["parameter_counts"]["trainable"],
                          "sec/epoch": RUNS[n]["seconds_per_epoch"]} for n in names])


def pick_best(names):
    """Validation-only selection: highest validation accuracy, lowest validation loss as tie-break."""
    return min(names, key=lambda n: (-RUNS[n]["best_val_accuracy"], RUNS[n]["best_val_loss"]))


def selection_note(names, chosen):
    """State the validation-only basis for a selection, naming the tie-break when it was needed."""
    accuracies = {name: round(RUNS[name]["best_val_accuracy"], 6) for name in names}
    if len(set(accuracies.values())) == 1:
        return (f"validation accuracy saturates at {accuracies[chosen]:.4f} for every condition, so the"
                f" tie-break applies: selected '{chosen}' on the lowest validation loss"
                f" ({RUNS[chosen]['best_val_loss']:.4f})")
    return f"selected '{chosen}' on the highest validation accuracy ({accuracies[chosen]:.4f})"


def inference_milliseconds(model, loader, repeats=5):
    """Mean forward-pass latency per image, measured on pre-loaded batches after a warm-up."""
    model.to(DEVICE).eval()
    batches = [images for images, _ in loader]
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(2):
            model(batches[0].to(DEVICE))
    if DEVICE.type == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
    started, total = time.perf_counter(), 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(repeats):
            for images in batches:
                model(images.to(DEVICE)); total += images.shape[0]
    if DEVICE.type == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return 1000.0 * (time.perf_counter() - started) / total


def test_report(run, *, loaders=None, class_names=None):
    """Evaluate a validation-selected run once on its held-out test split."""
    loaders = loaders or run["loaders"]
    names = list(class_names or run["class_names"])
    evaluation = sc.evaluate_model(run["model"], loaders["test"], nn.CrossEntropyLoss(), DEVICE)
    return evaluation, sc.classification_metrics(evaluation["labels"], evaluation["predictions"], names)


def per_class_table(metrics):
    return pd.DataFrame({"class": metrics["class_names"], "support": metrics["support"],
                         "precision": metrics["precision"], "recall": metrics["recall"],
                         "f1": metrics["f1"], "per_class_accuracy": metrics["per_class_accuracy"]})


def denormalize(tensor):
    """Undo ImageNet normalization so a transformed tensor can be displayed."""
    array = tensor.detach().cpu().numpy().transpose(1, 2, 0)
    return np.clip(array * np.array(sc.IMAGENET_STD) + np.array(sc.IMAGENET_MEAN), 0.0, 1.0)


def draw_confusion(ax, matrix, class_names, *, normalize=True, title="", annotate=None,
                   axis_labels=True):
    """Confusion matrix drawn into an existing axis (for multi-panel figures)."""
    shown = matrix.astype(float)
    if normalize:
        totals = shown.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        shown = np.divide(shown, totals, out=np.zeros_like(shown), where=totals > 0)
    ax.imshow(shown, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1 if normalize else max(shown.max(), 1))
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(class_names)), class_names, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(class_names)), class_names, fontsize=8)
    if axis_labels:
        ax.set_xlabel("predicted"); ax.set_ylabel("true")
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    annotate = len(class_names) <= 10 if annotate is None else annotate
    if annotate:
        for row in range(shown.shape[0]):
            for column in range(shown.shape[1]):
                ax.text(column, row, f"{shown[row, column]:.2f}" if normalize else int(matrix[row, column]),
                        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7,
                        color="white" if shown[row, column] > 0.6 * max(shown.max(), 1e-9) else "black")
    return ax


def external_label_counts(loader):
    """Per-class sample counts for a Hugging Face split, read from the label column only."""
    dataset = loader.dataset
    raw = dataset.split[dataset.label_column]
    if dataset.label_to_index is not None:
        indices = [dataset.label_to_index[value] for value in raw]
    else:
        indices = [int(value) for value in raw]
    return np.bincount(indices, minlength=len(dataset.class_names))


print("harness ready | device", DEVICE, "| batch", BATCH_SIZE, "| workers", NUM_WORKERS,
      "| epochs", EPOCHS, "| image size", sc.IMAGE_SIZE, "| seed", SEED)

Experiment 7 — robustness (3 points)¶

Apply one controlled degradation—Gaussian noise, blur, brightness, JPEG compression, or occlusion—to the test inputs without retraining. Compare original and degraded accuracy and save outputs/figures/robustness_results.png. Then save the selected model's final artifacts: its state dictionary as outputs/models/trained_model.pt (see a3_tools.save_state_dict) and outputs/tables/model_metadata.json using the README schema.

In [14]:
# --- controlled degradation: additive Gaussian pixel noise, no retraining ----------------------
NOISE_SIGMAS = [0.0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20]
noise_rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
clean_test = archive["test_images"].astype(np.float32)
test_labels = archive["test_labels"]


def noisy_test_loader(sigma):
    """Test loader with Gaussian noise applied in pixel space before the deterministic transform."""
    noisy = np.clip(clean_test + noise_rng.normal(0.0, sigma * 255.0, clean_test.shape), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    dataset = sc.ArrayImageDataset(noisy, test_labels, sc.evaluation_transform(), CLASS_NAMES)
    return DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False, num_workers=NUM_WORKERS), noisy


robustness, degraded_examples = [], {}
for sigma in NOISE_SIGMAS:
    loader, noisy_images = noisy_test_loader(sigma)
    evaluation = sc.evaluate_model(FINAL_RUN["model"], loader, nn.CrossEntropyLoss(), DEVICE)
    metrics = sc.classification_metrics(evaluation["labels"], evaluation["predictions"], CLASS_NAMES)
    degraded_examples[sigma] = noisy_images[0]
    robustness.append({"sigma": sigma, "accuracy": metrics["accuracy"], "loss": evaluation["loss"],
                       "macro_f1": metrics["macro_f1"],
                       "mean_confidence": float(evaluation["probabilities"].max(axis=1).mean())})
    condition = f"gaussian_noise_sigma={sigma:g}"
    record(7, "robustness to Gaussian pixel noise", condition, "test_accuracy", metrics["accuracy"], "fraction")
    record(7, "robustness to Gaussian pixel noise", condition, "test_loss", evaluation["loss"], "cross-entropy")
    record(7, "robustness to Gaussian pixel noise", condition, "test_macro_f1", metrics["macro_f1"], "fraction")
    record(7, "robustness to Gaussian pixel noise", condition, "mean_confidence",
           robustness[-1]["mean_confidence"], "probability")

robustness_table = pd.DataFrame(robustness)
clean_accuracy = robustness_table["accuracy"].iloc[0]
worst_accuracy = robustness_table["accuracy"].iloc[-1]
record(7, "robustness to Gaussian pixel noise", "original vs sigma=0.20", "accuracy_drop",
       clean_accuracy - worst_accuracy, "fraction")
print(robustness_table.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\noriginal {clean_accuracy:.4f} -> degraded (sigma=0.20) {worst_accuracy:.4f} "
      f"| drop {clean_accuracy - worst_accuracy:.4f}")

figure = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 4.8), dpi=130)
grid = figure.add_gridspec(1, 2, width_ratios=[1.0, 1.7], wspace=0.22)
axis = figure.add_subplot(grid[0, 0])
axis.plot(robustness_table["sigma"], robustness_table["accuracy"], "-o", color="#c44e52", label="test accuracy")
axis.plot(robustness_table["sigma"], robustness_table["mean_confidence"], "-s", color="#4c72b0",
          label="mean confidence")
axis.axhline(1.0 / NUM_CLASSES, ls=":", color="gray", label=f"chance ({1 / NUM_CLASSES:.2f})")
axis.set_xlabel("Gaussian noise sigma (fraction of dynamic range)"); axis.set_ylabel("value")
axis.set_ylim(0.0, 1.05); axis.grid(alpha=0.3); axis.legend(fontsize=9)
axis.set_title("Accuracy and confidence under degradation", fontsize=11)
inner = grid[0, 1].subgridspec(1, len(NOISE_SIGMAS), wspace=0.08)
for column, sigma in enumerate(NOISE_SIGMAS):
    tile = figure.add_subplot(inner[0, column])
    tile.imshow(degraded_examples[sigma]); tile.set_xticks([]); tile.set_yticks([])
    tile.set_title(f"sigma={sigma:g}\nacc {robustness_table['accuracy'].iloc[column]:.3f}", fontsize=9)
figure.suptitle("Experiment 7 - robustness of the validation-selected model to Gaussian pixel noise "
                "(no retraining)", fontsize=12)
figure.savefig(PATHS["figures"] / "robustness_results.png", bbox_inches="tight")

# --- final artifacts for the submitted model ---------------------------------------------------
checkpoint = a3_tools.save_state_dict(PATHS["models"] / "trained_model.pt", FINAL_RUN["model"])
size_mb = checkpoint.stat().st_size / 1e6
final_counts = a3_tools.parameter_counts(FINAL_RUN["model"])
model_metadata = {"architecture": FINAL_RUN["architecture"], "num_classes": NUM_CLASSES,
                  "class_names": CLASS_NAMES, "checkpoint": "outputs/models/trained_model.pt",
                  "parameter_counts": {"total": int(final_counts["total"]),
                                       "trainable": int(final_counts["trainable"])},
                  "seed": SEED, "selected_by": SELECTED_BY,
                  "training": {"mode": FINAL_RUN["mode"], "augmentation": FINAL_RUN["augmentation"],
                               "optimizer": FINAL_RUN["optimizer"], "learning_rate": FINAL_RUN["lr"],
                               "epochs": FINAL_RUN["epochs"], "selected_epoch": FINAL_RUN["best_epoch"],
                               "batch_size": BATCH_SIZE, "image_size": sc.IMAGE_SIZE},
                  "validation_accuracy": FINAL_RUN["best_val_accuracy"],
                  "test_accuracy": test_metrics["accuracy"]}
(PATHS["tables"] / "model_metadata.json").write_text(json.dumps(model_metadata, indent=2) + "\n")
print(f"\nsaved {checkpoint.name} ({size_mb:.1f} MB, state dictionary only, no optimizer state) "
      f"and model_metadata.json")
assert size_mb <= 25.0, f"checkpoint exceeds the 25 MB limit ({size_mb:.1f} MB)"
write_metrics().tail(3)
plt.close(figure)  # displayed once, as the cell result

7. Failure Analysis¶

Task 6 — two controlled failures (10 points)¶

Document two failures from different categories such as overfitting, underfitting, augmentation mismatch, label noise, domain shift, or systematic class confusion. For each: show evidence, explain the mechanism, apply a mitigation, and verify the change. Save one coherent outputs/figures/failure_analysis.png.

In [17]:
# =============================================================================================
# Failure A - LABEL NOISE driving OVERFITTING (memorization).
# 30% of the TRAINING labels are randomly reassigned while validation and test stay clean. The
# full backbone is fine-tuned, so the network has more than enough capacity to memorize the
# corrupted targets instead of learning the pattern, and validation accuracy falls.
# Mitigation: remove that capacity (freeze the backbone, head only) and add moderate
# augmentation, so the model can no longer fit the noise.
# =============================================================================================
LABEL_NOISE, FAILURE_EPOCHS = 0.30, 15


def noisy_label_loaders(fraction, augmentation, seed):
    """Loaders whose TRAIN labels are randomly corrupted; validation and test labels stay clean."""
    base = sc.build_dataloaders(a3_tools.dataset_path(), BATCH_SIZE, augmentation, seed, NUM_WORKERS)
    clean = base["train"].dataset.labels.copy()
    generator = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    chosen = generator.choice(len(clean), int(round(fraction * len(clean))), replace=False)
    noisy = clean.copy()
    noisy[chosen] = generator.integers(0, NUM_CLASSES, len(chosen))
    dataset = sc.ArrayImageDataset(archive["train_images"], noisy,
                                   base["train"].dataset.transform, CLASS_NAMES)
    base["train"] = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=True, num_workers=NUM_WORKERS,
                               generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed))
    return base, float((noisy != clean).mean())


noisy_loaders, actual_noise = noisy_label_loaders(LABEL_NOISE, "none", SEED)
print(f"training labels actually corrupted: {actual_noise:.1%} of 720 "
      f"(validation and test labels untouched)\n")
FAILURE_A = run_training("failA_label_noise_overfit", architecture=BEST_ARCHITECTURE, mode="finetune",
                         augmentation="none", optimizer_name="adam", lr=1e-3, epochs=FAILURE_EPOCHS,
                         seed=SEED, loaders=noisy_loaders, num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
                         class_names=CLASS_NAMES)
mitigated_loaders, _ = noisy_label_loaders(LABEL_NOISE, "moderate", SEED)
FAILURE_A_FIX = run_training("failA_mitigated", architecture=BEST_ARCHITECTURE, mode="frozen",
                             augmentation="moderate", optimizer_name="adam", lr=1e-3,
                             epochs=FAILURE_EPOCHS, seed=SEED, loaders=mitigated_loaders,
                             num_classes=NUM_CLASSES, class_names=CLASS_NAMES)
_, failure_a_metrics = test_report(FAILURE_A)
_, failure_a_fix_metrics = test_report(FAILURE_A_FIX)
# A model that learns only the true pattern predicts the true class, so it gets every unchanged
# label right and every changed label wrong: its training accuracy tops out at 1 - (changed
# fraction). Anything above it is memorization of the noise.
NOISE_CEILING = 1 - actual_noise
print(f"\nFailure A - {actual_noise:.1%} corrupted training labels (final-epoch values; "
      f"clean validation/test)")
print(f"  memorization-free training-accuracy ceiling ~ {NOISE_CEILING:.4f}")
print(f"  before: train {FAILURE_A['final_train_accuracy']:.4f} "
      f"({FAILURE_A['final_train_accuracy'] - NOISE_CEILING:+.4f} vs ceiling) / "
      f"val {FAILURE_A['final_val_accuracy']:.4f} -> gap {FAILURE_A['final_gap']:+.4f}"
      f" | clean test {failure_a_metrics['accuracy']:.4f} | trainable "
      f"{FAILURE_A['parameter_counts']['trainable']:,}")
print(f"  after : train {FAILURE_A_FIX['final_train_accuracy']:.4f} "
      f"({FAILURE_A_FIX['final_train_accuracy'] - NOISE_CEILING:+.4f} vs ceiling) / "
      f"val {FAILURE_A_FIX['final_val_accuracy']:.4f} -> gap {FAILURE_A_FIX['final_gap']:+.4f}"
      f" | clean test {failure_a_fix_metrics['accuracy']:.4f} | trainable "
      f"{FAILURE_A_FIX['parameter_counts']['trainable']:,}")
print(f"  verified change: validation accuracy "
      f"{FAILURE_A_FIX['final_val_accuracy'] - FAILURE_A['final_val_accuracy']:+.4f}, "
      f"clean test accuracy {failure_a_fix_metrics['accuracy'] - failure_a_metrics['accuracy']:+.4f}, "
      f"train-validation gap {FAILURE_A_FIX['final_gap'] - FAILURE_A['final_gap']:+.4f}")

# =============================================================================================
# Failure B - AUGMENTATION MISMATCH: 90-degree rotations rewrite the orientation classes, so
# `horizontal` and `vertical` become the same training distribution.
# Mitigation: drop the rotation and keep only the label-preserving flips/jitter.
# =============================================================================================
ROTATION_TRANSFORM = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize((sc.IMAGE_SIZE, sc.IMAGE_SIZE)),
    transforms.RandomChoice([transforms.RandomRotation((angle, angle)) for angle in (0, 90, 180, 270)]),
    transforms.ToTensor(), transforms.Normalize(sc.IMAGENET_MEAN, sc.IMAGENET_STD)])


def rotated_loaders(seed):
    """Loaders whose TRAIN transform adds label-destroying 90-degree rotations."""
    base = sc.build_dataloaders(a3_tools.dataset_path(), BATCH_SIZE, "none", seed, NUM_WORKERS)
    dataset = sc.ArrayImageDataset(archive["train_images"], archive["train_labels"],
                                   ROTATION_TRANSFORM, CLASS_NAMES)
    base["train"] = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=True, num_workers=NUM_WORKERS,
                               generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed))
    return base


FAILURE_B = run_training("failB_rotation_mismatch", architecture=BEST_ARCHITECTURE, mode="finetune",
                         augmentation="rot90", optimizer_name="adam", epochs=8, seed=SEED,
                         loaders=rotated_loaders(SEED), num_classes=NUM_CLASSES, class_names=CLASS_NAMES)
FAILURE_B_FIX = run_training("failB_mitigated", architecture=BEST_ARCHITECTURE, mode="finetune",
                             augmentation="moderate", optimizer_name="adam", epochs=8, seed=SEED,
                             num_classes=NUM_CLASSES, class_names=CLASS_NAMES)
_, failure_b_metrics = test_report(FAILURE_B)
_, failure_b_fix_metrics = test_report(FAILURE_B_FIX)
ORIENTED = [CLASS_NAMES.index("horizontal"), CLASS_NAMES.index("vertical")]
confusion_before = failure_b_metrics["confusion_matrix"]
confusion_after = failure_b_fix_metrics["confusion_matrix"]
swap = lambda matrix: int(matrix[ORIENTED[0], ORIENTED[1]] + matrix[ORIENTED[1], ORIENTED[0]])
oriented_accuracy = lambda metrics: float(np.mean([metrics["per_class_accuracy"][i] for i in ORIENTED]))
print(f"\nFailure B (90-degree rotation augmentation destroys orientation labels)")
print(f"  before: test accuracy {failure_b_metrics['accuracy']:.4f} | horizontal/vertical accuracy "
      f"{oriented_accuracy(failure_b_metrics):.4f} | mutual confusions {swap(confusion_before)}")
print(f"  after : test accuracy {failure_b_fix_metrics['accuracy']:.4f} | horizontal/vertical accuracy "
      f"{oriented_accuracy(failure_b_fix_metrics):.4f} | mutual confusions {swap(confusion_after)}")
print(f"  verified change: accuracy {failure_b_fix_metrics['accuracy'] - failure_b_metrics['accuracy']:+.4f}, "
      f"mutual confusions {swap(confusion_after) - swap(confusion_before):+d}")

for experiment_label, before, after, before_metrics, after_metrics in (
        ("failure_A_label_noise_overfitting", FAILURE_A, FAILURE_A_FIX, failure_a_metrics, failure_a_fix_metrics),
        ("failure_B_augmentation_mismatch", FAILURE_B, FAILURE_B_FIX, failure_b_metrics, failure_b_fix_metrics)):
    for stage, run, metrics in (("before_mitigation", before, before_metrics),
                                ("after_mitigation", after, after_metrics)):
        condition = f"{experiment_label}/{stage}"
        record("task6", "failure analysis", condition, "final_train_accuracy", run["final_train_accuracy"], "fraction")
        record("task6", "failure analysis", condition, "final_val_accuracy", run["final_val_accuracy"], "fraction")
        record("task6", "failure analysis", condition, "best_val_accuracy", run["best_val_accuracy"], "fraction")
        record("task6", "failure analysis", condition, "final_train_val_gap", run["final_gap"], "fraction")
        record("task6", "failure analysis", condition, "test_accuracy", metrics["accuracy"], "fraction")
        record("task6", "failure analysis", condition, "test_macro_f1", metrics["macro_f1"], "fraction")
record("task6", "failure analysis", "failure_A_label_noise_overfitting", "corrupted_label_fraction",
       actual_noise, "fraction")
record("task6", "failure analysis", "failure_A_label_noise_overfitting",
       "memorization_free_train_ceiling", NOISE_CEILING, "fraction")
record("task6", "failure analysis", "failure_A_label_noise_overfitting", "gap_reduction",
       FAILURE_A["final_gap"] - FAILURE_A_FIX["final_gap"], "fraction")
record("task6", "failure analysis", "failure_A_label_noise_overfitting", "clean_test_accuracy_gain",
       failure_a_fix_metrics["accuracy"] - failure_a_metrics["accuracy"], "fraction")
record("task6", "failure analysis", "failure_B_augmentation_mismatch", "oriented_class_accuracy_gain",
       oriented_accuracy(failure_b_fix_metrics) - oriented_accuracy(failure_b_metrics), "fraction")
record("task6", "failure analysis", "failure_B_augmentation_mismatch", "horizontal_vertical_confusions_before",
       swap(confusion_before), "count")
record("task6", "failure analysis", "failure_B_augmentation_mismatch", "horizontal_vertical_confusions_after",
       swap(confusion_after), "count")

# --- failure_analysis.png ----------------------------------------------------------------------
figure, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10), dpi=120)
for axis, run, title in ((axes[0, 0], FAILURE_A,
                          f"A - {actual_noise:.1%} corrupted training labels, full fine-tuning\n"
                          f"(4.0M trainable weights can memorize them)"),
                         (axes[0, 1], FAILURE_A_FIX,
                          "A - mitigated: frozen backbone + moderate augmentation\n"
                          "(too few trainable weights to memorize)")):
    history = run["history"]
    axis.plot(history["epoch"], history["train_accuracy"], "-o", ms=3, color="#4c72b0", label="train accuracy")
    axis.plot(history["epoch"], history["val_accuracy"], "-s", ms=3, color="#c44e52", label="validation accuracy")
    axis.fill_between(history["epoch"], history["val_accuracy"], history["train_accuracy"],
                      color="#c44e52", alpha=0.12, label="train - validation")
    axis.axhline(NOISE_CEILING, ls="--", lw=1.2, color="#555555",
                 label=f"memorization-free train ceiling ({NOISE_CEILING:.2f})")
    axis.set_title(f"{title}, final train-val gap {run['final_gap']:+.3f}", fontsize=10)
    axis.set_xlabel("epoch"); axis.set_ylabel("accuracy"); axis.set_ylim(0.4, 1.05)
    axis.grid(alpha=0.3); axis.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
draw_confusion(axes[1, 0], confusion_before, CLASS_NAMES, normalize=True,
               title=f"B - 90-degree rotation augmentation\ntest accuracy {failure_b_metrics['accuracy']:.3f}, "
                     f"horizontal/vertical confusions {swap(confusion_before)}")
draw_confusion(axes[1, 1], confusion_after, CLASS_NAMES, normalize=True,
               title=f"B - mitigated: rotation removed\ntest accuracy {failure_b_fix_metrics['accuracy']:.3f}, "
                     f"horizontal/vertical confusions {swap(confusion_after)}")
figure.suptitle("Task 6 - two controlled failures with evidence, mitigation, and verification", fontsize=13)
figure.tight_layout()
figure.savefig(PATHS["figures"] / "failure_analysis.png", bbox_inches="tight")
print("\nsaved", (PATHS["figures"] / "failure_analysis.png").name)
write_metrics().tail(3)
plt.close(figure)  # displayed once, as the cell result

Task 7 — Extension (10 points)¶

Choose Grad-CAM, saliency, MixUp, CutMix, a cosine scheduler, label smoothing, knowledge distillation, or an approved recognition enhancement. Submit one artifact under outputs/extension/, one controlled baseline comparison, and a concise evidence-based conclusion. Use no additional packages or externally pretrained pipeline.

# ============================================================================================
# Extension: LABEL SMOOTHING (epsilon = 0.1) against an otherwise identical baseline.
# Question: does label smoothing change held-out accuracy, or only confidence calibration?
# Controlled: identical architecture, mode, augmentation, optimizer, lr, loaders, seed, epochs;
# the training loss function is the only difference, and both are evaluated with plain
# cross-entropy on the same splits.
# ============================================================================================
SMOOTHING = 0.1
EXTENSION_RUNS = {}
for label, epsilon in (("baseline_ce", 0.0), (f"label_smoothing_{SMOOTHING:g}", SMOOTHING)):
    EXTENSION_RUNS[label] = run_training(f"ext_{label}", epochs=EPOCHS, seed=SEED,
                                         label_smoothing=epsilon, **SELECTED_CONFIG)

extension_rows = []
for label, run in EXTENSION_RUNS.items():
    evaluation, metrics = test_report(run)
    confidence = evaluation["probabilities"].max(axis=1)
    correct = evaluation["predictions"] == evaluation["labels"]
    row = {"condition": label, "label_smoothing": run["label_smoothing"],
           "best_val_accuracy": run["best_val_accuracy"], "test_accuracy": metrics["accuracy"],
           "test_macro_f1": metrics["macro_f1"], "test_loss": evaluation["loss"],
           "mean_confidence": float(confidence.mean()),
           "mean_confidence_correct": float(confidence[correct].mean()) if correct.any() else float("nan"),
           "mean_confidence_wrong": float(confidence[~correct].mean()) if (~correct).any() else float("nan"),
           "overconfidence_gap": float(confidence.mean() - metrics["accuracy"])}
    extension_rows.append(row)
    EXTENSION_RUNS[label] = {**run, "confidence": confidence, "correct": correct,
                             "metrics": metrics, "evaluation": evaluation}
    for metric in ("best_val_accuracy", "test_accuracy", "test_macro_f1", "mean_confidence",
                   "overconfidence_gap"):
        record("task7", "extension: label smoothing", label, metric, row[metric],
               "cross-entropy" if metric == "test_loss" else "fraction")

extension_table = pd.DataFrame(extension_rows)
baseline, smoothed = extension_rows[0], extension_rows[1]
record("task7", "extension: label smoothing", "smoothed minus baseline", "test_accuracy_delta",
       smoothed["test_accuracy"] - baseline["test_accuracy"], "fraction")
record("task7", "extension: label smoothing", "smoothed minus baseline", "overconfidence_gap_delta",
       smoothed["overconfidence_gap"] - baseline["overconfidence_gap"], "fraction")
print(extension_table.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\ntest accuracy {baseline['test_accuracy']:.4f} -> {smoothed['test_accuracy']:.4f} "
      f"({smoothed['test_accuracy'] - baseline['test_accuracy']:+.4f}) | "
      f"overconfidence gap {baseline['overconfidence_gap']:+.4f} -> {smoothed['overconfidence_gap']:+.4f} "
      f"({smoothed['overconfidence_gap'] - baseline['overconfidence_gap']:+.4f})")

# --- outputs/extension/label_smoothing_comparison.png ------------------------------------------
figure, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.8), dpi=130)
palette = {"baseline_ce": "#999999", f"label_smoothing_{SMOOTHING:g}": "#4c72b0"}
for label, run in EXTENSION_RUNS.items():
    history = run["history"]
    axes[0].plot(history["epoch"], history["val_accuracy"], "-o", ms=4, color=palette[label], label=label)
axes[0].set_xlabel("epoch"); axes[0].set_ylabel("validation accuracy"); axes[0].set_ylim(0, 1.03)

for label, run in EXTENSION_RUNS.items():

10. Submission Validation¶

Restart the kernel, run all cells, and export current HTML as A3.html. Then run:

python /path/to/common-setup/scripts/validate_submission.py --assignment A3
python /path/to/common-setup/scripts/package_submission.py --assignment A3

Submit LastName_FirstName_A3.zip. Do not submit PDF, dataset or pretrained-weight copies, caches, environments, experiment-tracking directories, or nested ZIP files.

Canvas submission checklist¶

  • The ZIP contains exactly one top-level folder named LastName_FirstName_A3.
  • Section 0 identity fields (first name, last name, ABC123) are complete.
  • A3.ipynb was restarted, run top to bottom, and saved without errors, and A3.html was exported after that final run.
  • src/ contains the required source files: a3_tools.py and student_code.py.
  • outputs/ contains only the required figures, tables, the trained_model.pt checkpoint (state dictionary only, no optimizer state, ≤25 MB), and one extension artifact — no extra files.
  • python scripts/validate_submission.py --assignment A3 reports zero errors; review any warnings.
  • No datasets, pretrained-weight copies, environments, caches, extra checkpoints, hidden files, or temporary files are included.
  • External resources and meaningful generative-AI use are disclosed in Section 0.
  • A PDF export is not required and is not included.
